extra.message: registrySignIn() implements a second, parallel authentication path that verifies credentials using a raw MD5 digest of the supplied phrase compared against the stored passwordHash, instead of the BCryptPasswordEncoder used everywhere else (login(), resetPassword()). MD5 has no work factor and is unsuitable for password verification; worse, if a user record has no passwordHash yet, the first caller's MD5(phrase) is silently persisted as the permanent password hash (lines 91-93), letting anyone who reaches this endpoint first claim the account's credential.

extra.message: corsConfigurationSource() sets 'setAllowedOriginPatterns(List.of("*"))' together with 'setAllowCredentials(true)' for the '/api/**' path. Spring's allowedOriginPatterns (unlike allowedOrigins) permits the literal wildcard to be combined with credentials: the filter reflects whatever Origin header the browser sends and still allows cookies to be included. Any external website can therefore issue credentialed cross-origin requests (fetch with credentials:'include') to endpoints like /api/matter-search and /api/workspace-view on behalf of a logged-in victim and read the JSON response, leaking matter data or changing the victim's effective view role cross-origin.
